links.note: The task is to identify countries that have a federal system - the answer names USA, Brazil and Australia. That is 24058 (each level with its own jurisdiction, neither subordinate), against 24057 the unitary alternative. 24059 would be needed only if the item asked how those federations came about.

The similarity the answer identifies is that in both countries power is divided among a national government, provincial/state governments and a local or community government - i.e. the multi-level structure, 24055. 24069 covers only India's third tier.

The stem's discriminating term is 'unitary', and 24057 is the concept the chapter introduces solely for this contrast (one level, or sub-units subordinate to the centre). The federal half of the answer is 24058, which many other items in this chapter reach on their own.

The two differences the answer gives are exactly 24071: elections to local bodies became constitutionally mandatory, and seats were reserved for SCs, STs, OBCs and women. 24069 is the general principle of decentralisation; this item asks what the 1992 amendment changed.
Fill-in of 'coming together' for the USA and 'holding together' for India, with strong states in the first and a stronger centre in the second - 24059's description entirely.

Three positions on India's language policy; the answer argues from the decision to continue English alongside Hindi and to impose no language. 24067. 24066 Linguistic states is the sibling that Arman's position invokes, but the item is about the language policy.
Groups nine subjects across all three lists. 24064 carries two of the three (State and Concurrent), so the item sits there; 24063 covers only the Union column.
The mismatched pair is 'local governments - residuary powers', and the answer states residuary powers belong to the Union. 24065 exactly.

Matches one head of government to each level - Prime Minister to the Union, Governor to the state, Mayor to a municipal corporation, Sarpanch to a gram panchayat. The item's organising idea is the tiers themselves, 24055; the two local pairs reach into 24069/24070 but neither covers the Union and state pairs.

The two keyed-correct statements are that a federation's powers are clearly demarcated and that India's Union and State governments have exclusive jurisdiction over their subjects - 24060's description. 24061 is the sibling (the division being constitutionally entrenched), which statement B touches only in passing. India as the example of a holding-together federation, against the coming-together cases (USA, Switzerland, Australia). 24059.
Power taken from central and state governments and given to local government is 24069's description word for word.
Both levels legislating on the same subjects is the Concurrent List, which 24064 carries. 24063 is the Union List only.
Law and order as the odd one out against foreign affairs, currency and banking - the Union List's contents, 24063. Law and order is a State List subject, so the item turns on knowing the Union List.
Australia as federal against Egypt, Sri Lanka and England, which are unitary. The federal-versus-unitary distinction is 24058/24057; the stem asks which HAS a federal form, so 24058.
Identifies the head of government at the state level, i.e. the second of the federal system's levels - 24055.
Japan as the one that did not form by holding together (it is unitary), against India, Spain and Belgium. 24059.
'Two or more levels' is 24055's defining property of a federal government, against community, coalition and unitary governments.
Marriage as a Concurrent List subject against Defence and Currency (Union) and Agriculture (State). 24064.
India as a holding-together federation against USA, Australia and Switzerland, the coming-together cases. 24059.

Jammu and Kashmir's special status is the chapter's illustration that in a holding-together federation some units have more power than others - 24059, not 24061, which is about the division being unchangeable unilaterally.
The incorrect statement is 'one-fourth of positions reserved for women' - the amendment reserved at least one-third. All four options are the 1992 amendment's provisions, which is 24071.

Parliament cannot alone alter the centre-state arrangement: a two-thirds majority in both Houses plus ratification by half the state legislatures. That is 24061's 'cannot be changed unilaterally' exactly.
Switzerland as the odd one out because it came together rather than held together. 24059.

The Constitution originally providing a two-tier system, before the third tier was added, is 24055. 24069 covers the later addition of the local tier, which this stem explicitly excludes by saying 'originally'.
The incorrect statement is that a state government is answerable to the centre - 24058's 'neither is subordinate'. 24057 is the unitary case where that statement would be true.

Federalism identified as the vertical division of power between a central authority and constituent units - 24054's definition. The horizontal, community and party forms are the distractors from the power-sharing forms.
Defence, foreign affairs, banking, currency and communications is the Union List enumeration in 24063; the distractors are the Concurrent, State and residuary sets.
Jammu and Kashmir having its own Constitution is the same unequal-powers point as qid:105439 in the holding-together discussion, 24059.
Same three positions as qid:87396, keyed to accommodation strengthening national unity - the language policy, 24067.
